quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol with the medication.
Have the same effect on all people.

questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal) can have side effects that reduce your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: The best way to stop quickly is to:

options.text: Close the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, press both brakes at the same time with firm pressure. Do not panic if the brakes lock.

questions.question: When you cannot avoid an object or uneven surface, you should:

options.text: Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rise off the seat so your legs can absorb the impact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, approach it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as possible and keep the motorcycle upright. Rise off the seat so your knees can absorb the shock. Just before impact, roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the operator:
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals when they do not have turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the operator plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to increase your visibility?

options.text: Using your headlight at all times

questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials, use your headlight at all times, and use your turn signals and brake light correctly.

questions.question: Use your mirrors when stopped at an intersection to:

options.text: See if parked vehicles are entering traffic.
Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
See if someone is turning behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for vehicles behind you that may not be stopping.
questions.explanation: When stopped at an intersection, check your mirrors to see vehicles approaching from behind. The drivers might not see you until they are too close, so you may need to react quickly.

questions.question: During acceleration, a sidecar attached to a motorcycle will:

options.text: Feel like it is falling behind.
Feel like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is falling behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of its weight, it will feel like it is falling behind when you accelerate.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should:
questions.explanation: Staggered riding is usually best, but switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?
questions.explanation: The throttle is usually on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—it will make the motorcycle less stable. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, what should they do?

options.text: Pass in a staggered formation with several riders at once.
Pass one rider at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass one rider at a time.
questions.explanation: When a group of motorcyclists passes another vehicle on a two-lane road, each rider must pass one at a time. Each rider must finish their pass before the next rider begins.

questions.question: What does an experienced rider do?

options.text: Changes position within their lane based on road conditions.
Stays in the same spot in the lane at all times.
Weaves within the lane to be more visible.
Rides only on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Changes position within their lane based on road conditions.
questions.explanation: A motorcyclist has three position choices within their lane. An experienced rider picks the safest position based on current road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When someone tailgates you, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore them and focus on the road ahead.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride on the shoulder and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster and increase danger. Never ride on the shoulder—drivers will not expect you there and may suddenly leave the road.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Apply them at the same time for the best stopping power.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: It means the driver sees you.
It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you properly.
It guarantees the driver will yield to you properly.
It may make the driver angry.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not guarantee the driver will yield to you properly.
questions.explanation: Never assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but still fail to see them.

questions.question: Which of these can be a rectangular sign?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs, such as speed limit signs, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Riders must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What should your lane position do?

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should give you a way to escape if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you assume?

options.text: Other drivers see you as easily as they see other vehicles.
You do not need to worry about being seen.

questions.explanation: Motorcycles are small and have fewer lights than other vehicles, making them hard to see. For safety, ride defensively and assume that other drivers do not see you.

questions.question: When riding at night, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to avoid collisions. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam headlight, but switch to low beam when following or meeting other vehicles.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles moving in the same direction?

options.text: Yes, during the day to reduce traffic jams.
Yes, if the rider feels comfortable doing it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot ride between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street.

questions.question: Where is the horn button on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for at least one hour.
After riding for more than 8 hours.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts riding.

questions.question: What is the correct way to pass another vehicle?

options.text: You must stay within the speed limit while passing.
You can finish a pass in a no passing zone if you started before entering it.
You can exceed the speed limit while passing.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stay within the speed limit while passing.
questions.explanation: All passes must be completed within the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: How can you keep another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Move side to side within your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it.
